Resolutions:
- tests/cek-executor.staged-route.test.ts: the branch's content (its

- The branch's staged-builtin test files and test helpers build their

Describe the reconciliation-only staging hold at the prepare holder

Prove a division by zero past the direct bound through the executor

Also rewrap the staged builtins module doc to the line limit.
Cover all-ones operands in the hop cost model and return an indeterminate plan when no column fits
Pin the staged product result's leading byte and zero memory with refusal rows

Pin the staged operand binding and the conversion input bound

Rows that claim the correct value of what is actually staged, so each is
refused only by the check it names:
- byteStringToInteger with different bytes of the same length staged in
  place of the input, claiming the staged bytes' value, in both byte orders;
- verifyEd25519Signature and verifySchnorrSecp256k1Signature with another
  message of the same length staged in place of the argument, claiming the
  valid signature over the staged message;
- byteStringToInteger over 65,537 bytes whose value is 7, claiming 7: big
  endian, little endian and in three pieces, with the same shapes at 65,536
  bytes accepted.

Refresh interactive-emulator durations for the staged-step files

Records one local forks-1 run for the staged-step files whose entries had
drifted and adds entries for the files the removal-by-another-record
rows and the merged own-thread reclaim files added.

Spend back staging outputs when another record resolves the case

A staged step's staging outputs stayed at our staging address once the
block was removed against another record: the resolution reached the run
before the staging sweep, so no spend back went out. The staging wrapper
now sits outside the own-thread reclaim, so a thread of ours is cancelled
first and the sweep then sees the resolution, whether it is raised or
observed as a terminal our journal did not create. It spends each staging
output back and holds the ending as outstanding until each spend back is
final at release depth.

Under reconciliation-only authority the sweep keeps holding the outputs a
thread of ours past the PrepareSelected move holds, until that thread
leaves its holders. When the thread committed evidence and no staging is
found, the staged-step plan now refuses, and the run raises the one-step
alarm each time instead of building without the staging.
